result.competitor: The free state platform elevator.mindev.gov.gr does the core job at no cost. Elevator maintainers and installers are allowed to file on owners' behalf and have to, because they cannot lawfully complete maintenance on an unregistered lift. Until July 2027 they can also file late registrations without a fine. I found no commercial Greek software for this, and none for common-expense or building management that bundles it, but there is little need for one.
result.duty: Art. 11A of Law 3982/2011, as amended by Art. 137 of Law 5317/2026 (in force). Owners, building administrators or legal representatives must register every installed elevator in the Elevator Census Register (elevator.mindev.gov.gr, Taxisnet login, free). The required data are address, KAEK, stops, installation year and maintainer. Maintainers and installers may also file. The deadline was 30 Jun 2026, after one extension, and is a one-off; data corrections and new installations continue. New elevators: the installer registers within 90 days of the CE declaration, with no fine. Late fines per elevator are EUR 1,000 (residential), EUR 2,500 (commercial or mixed use) and EUR 5,000 (buildings open to the public). Until 10 Jul 2027, a maintainer or installer can register a late elevator without a fine, given a declaration from one owner or the administrator. Regular maintenance of an elevator with no registration number cannot lawfully be completed, except work needed to make it safe. Sanctions under the 2008 joint ministerial decision on certification are suspended until the data moves to the unified Register, and no certification timetable has been set. I did not confirm that fines have actually been issued.
result.market: ELSTAT (via To Vima) estimates about 310,000 installed elevators. 263,087 had been registered by 30 Nov 2025 and 286,324 by 19 Jun 2026, which leaves roughly 24k (about 8%) unregistered, and the 2027 window lets maintainers register those without a fine. I did not find a count of building administrators or of how many unregistered lifts are in small buildings.
result.reason: The duty is real. Art. 11A of Law 3982/2011, as amended by Art. 137 of Law 5317/2026, sets fines of EUR 1,000, 2,500 or 5,000 per elevator. But the core job is a short one-off form on the free state platform elevator.mindev.gov.gr, and maintainers or installers may file it. About 286k of roughly 310k elevators were registered by 19 Jun 2026. Until 10 Jul 2027, maintainers can register the remaining late elevators without a fine if they have one owner's declaration. Lift companies already have to do this, because routine maintenance of an unregistered lift cannot lawfully be completed. Penalties under the old certification rules are suspended, and no new certification timetable has been set. The census is mostly over, and what is left falls naturally to maintainers.

result.competitor: Free state portal elevator.mindev.gov.gr (Ministry of Development lift census registry, live since 1 Aug 2025) handles registration and maintainer data; maintainers log in with Taxisnet. Census number on invoices can be added with a custom field in existing Greek invoicing/ERP software (no specific product named). Generic foreign lift-maintenance field-service tools found: Shifton (shifton.com), Caction (caction.com), FieldBoss Elevator 365, Field Force Tracker. No Greek-language vertical lift-maintenance software found in 4 Greek searches.
result.duty: Law 3982/2011 Art. 11A(5) as replaced by Law 5317/2026 Art. 137: owner, manager or legal representative must register each lift on the Ministry of Development registry (maintainer or installer may file). Maintainer/installer must confirm the census number during routine work and write it on the tax invoice for maintenance; omission or a plainly wrong number is an administrative offence (fine amount for maintainers not found). Routine maintenance cannot lawfully be completed on an unregistered lift. Late registration by maintainer without fine until 10 July 2027, with a sworn statement from an owner. Installer must register new lifts within 90 days of the CE declaration. Owner fines are EUR 1,000, 2,500 or 5,000 per lift, depending on building use. Not confirmed: whether registry modules for maintenance assignment, take-over, change of firm and maintenance logs (2026 draft) are in force. Workshop licence lasts 5 years (mitos.gov.gr).
result.market: Not found: no official count of licensed lift maintenance workshops (the register is kept by the Regional Development Directorates). Context: an estimated 700,000-900,000 lifts in Greece; around 200,000 registered by Nov 2025 (in.gr). The claim's figure of about 7,000 maintainers comes from a parliamentary question and was not verified.
result.reason: The maintainer duty is real but thin. Art. 137 of Law 5317/2026, amending Art. 11A of Law 3982/2011, requires maintainers to confirm the census number, print it on every invoice (leaving it off is an administrative offence) and refuse routine maintenance on unregistered lifts. Registration is filed on the free state portal elevator.mindev.gov.gr with Taxisnet login. The duty is per invoice, so an existing invoicing tool with a custom field covers it. I could not confirm that the assign/take-over/maintenance-log functions from the draft are in force. I found no Greek vertical software, but generic foreign lift-maintenance tools exist (Shifton, Caction). The number of licensed firms was not found. One opening: until 10 July 2027 maintainers can register unregistered lifts without a fine.

result.competitor: Registry filing goes through AADE's free registry app and the my1521 portal. I found no standalone Greek product for the registry itself. The input-output core job is done by ministry-listed installers and software makers whose systems connect to AADE. The installer list is kept by the Development Ministry (mitos.gov.gr). I named no specific vendor because none appeared in results, so whether installers offer registry filing as a service is unverified. The likely bundling with installers is the main threat.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force. A.1180/2025 (live since 23/12/2025, circular E.2112/2025) and A.1200/2026 require an electronic census of tanks in AADE's Tank Registry. A.1202/2026 (amending A.1176/2024) requires input-output systems to be installed or upgraded. The 02/10/2026 joint ministry and AADE release moved the deadlines to 31/12/2027 for private stations and the registry; public stations have until 30/06/2027 in Attica and Thessaloniki and 31/12/2027 elsewhere. Obligors are holders of private-use licences under Law 3784/2009 art. 31 par. 7a, plus accredited gauging bodies and installers, which also file in the registry. The registry is mostly one-off; tanks must be re-gauged every 10 years (KYA F2-1617/2010). I found no penalty amount in the 2026 sources, so the 15,000 EUR figure is unverified. The release mentions a voucher of up to 3,000 EUR.
result.market: Not found. No source gave a count of private-use stations or licences. The holders are spread across hauliers, construction machinery fleets, KTEL bus operators, marinas, ports and storage depots. Licences are issued by the regional transport directorates, and I found no public register count.
result.reason: The duty is real but weak for a SaaS. A joint ministry and AADE release of 02/10/2026 sets a deadline of 31/12/2027 for the Tank Registry (A.1200/2026) and for input-output systems at private stations (A.1202/2026). The registry is mainly a one-off census on AADE's own app. Installers and accredited gauging bodies must also file, so the people who already install the hardware probably handle it. The continuous input-output monitoring has to run on equipment and software from manufacturers and installers listed by the ministry, so a solo founder cannot easily build it. With the deadline 14 months away, urgency is low. I found no count of private-use stations and no named vendor. The 15,000 EUR fine was not confirmed; the one hit was a 2023 profiteering fine.

Duty is real: L.5259/2025 art.180 (new paras 12A-12D, 13A of Art.52 VAT Code) creates an AADE register with a unique trader number for margin-scheme resellers and for non-VAT buyers. Strike-off for 3 years follows an audit finding. There is no fine, no recurring reporting, and the record holds only name and tax ID. The start date and operating decision were not found, and I found no sign the register has opened. It is mostly a one-off registration done in a free AADE portal. Software could add little beyond ordinary invoicing and ERP margin-scheme invoices. Market size was not found. No competitor was found, but the duty is thin.

result.duty: Monthly electronic declaration and payment of the Climate Crisis Resilience Fee (ΤΑΚΚ), due the last day of the following month. Penalties fall under Law 5104/2024 arts. 52-53.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. The Climate Resilience Fee (Law 5104/2024) replaced the accommodation levy. Operators file a monthly declaration on myAADE, due the last day of the following month. The seasonal window I did not confirm. The claim says March-October, but the Skai article gives April-October for short-term rentals and a winter rate for November-March. AADE's Feb 2026 FAQ lists furnished rooms and apartments, short-term rentals and villas as liable. The filing is a simple free state portal form, and accountants can file for clients. The core job is therefore trivial and already served by AADE's portal, accountants and PMS tools. I did not find a dedicated fee-calculator product, but the pain is low. It is the same buyer group as rejected K11. I did not check penalty amounts or market size. Rates conflict between sources.

Duty is real: the I/O monitoring rule (KYA F2-1617/2010, amended F2-2022/2012) covers heating-oil seller installations. An AADE release (23 Mar 2026) lists heating-oil sellers as obligors, extends full adaptation to 31 Dec 2026, and cites A.1073/2026. I could not open the 2 Oct 2026 AADE PDF (403), so the A.1202/2026 text and any separate seller deadline are unconfirmed. It also looks like a hardware/certified-installer job, since AADE requires software declarations from vendors. The market size is not found. Penalties were not checked. The buyers are few, regional licence holders, and the work is mostly hardware, so a solo-founder software play is weak.

result.duty: Charter parties, crew and passenger lists must be submitted electronically via e-Ναυλοσύμφωνο (KYA 3133.1/47821/2024, law 4256/2014). Penalty and exact frequency not verified.
result.market: About 6,109 professional pleasure craft in 2019 and about 6,500 in a newmoney.gr estimate, with 200 to 300 added per year. Not a current register figure.
result.reason: The duty is real. The Ministry of Maritime Affairs e-Ναυλοσύμφωνο went live on 14 May 2026 at echarterparty.yna.gov.gr under KYA 3133.1/47821/2024, with a transition to 30 June 2026. I could not confirm that date, the KYA number or the extension status from an official ministry source, and I did not check the stay fee or crew rules. The core job is already covered. The state portal does the submission, and Booking Manager and CaptainBook both export charter party and crew data to it. Booking Manager and CaptainBook are mainly sold to charter fleets and are integrated into their booking tools, so small operators are already served. Market size is about 6,100 to 6,500 professional pleasure craft (2019 estimate, not a current register count). Willingness to pay is likely low. A bolt-on would be a thin add-on to existing tools.

The duty is real. Law 5092/2024 requires concession holders to display a QR signage plate, and omitting it is fined. Free access for the public and minimum gaps from neighbours are also required, with fines of 2,000 to 60,000 EUR for blocking access. KYA 11996 EX/2026 (FEK B 283) was amended by 43966 EX/2026 (FEK B 1490), 68113 EX/2026 and 92618 EX/2026, but it covers only applications for simple use of seashore by adjacent businesses and sports clubs. The state already does the core job for free. The minfin portal publishes each concession's QR code, and holders download it with Taxisnet login (Kalamata municipal notice). Concessions are issued by e-auction and by the state platform. No dedicated private compliance software turned up, only QR-menu and POS tools for beach bars. The duty is mostly annual and seasonal, not a recurring workflow, and thin to automate. I did not verify the 6,500-concession count, who files, or the penalty amounts.

The duty is real. Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 applies from 30 Dec 2026 to large and medium operators and from 30 Jun 2027 to micro and small ones. Sources disagree on whether small timber operators already under the EUTR must comply from Dec 2026. The 4 May 2026 review kept the text unchanged and promised no further delay. Weak points: (1) downstream traders after the first one need not file a DDS, which removes most small Greek roasters and furniture shops; (2) micro and small primary operators file only a one-time simplified declaration; (3) the draft delegated act would remove leather from scope; (4) international SaaS (osapiens, TraceX) exists, though I found no Greek-language vendor; (5) I did not find the Greek competent authority, penalties or an operator count. Likely a small market with low pain.

Duty is real: per the Almopia municipal notice (June 2026), premises still on an old licence must complete the OPS-ADE census and notification under art. 14A of law 4442/2016 and art. 59 of law 5525/2025 by 31-12-2026. After that date a 200 EUR fee applies. Art. 14B document upload has the same deadline. I found no later extension, but I didn't check the primary text or a gazette. The state OPS-ADE portal, KEPs, accountants and engineers already do the job, and I found no private software. The duty is one-off, so a service fits better than software. Premises count unknown and unquantified. Fragmented buyers, low willingness to pay, and a free state tool make this a weak SaaS case.

Duty confirmed: the EAE 2026 is filed only on AADE's free myAGRO platform. It opened on 4 Aug 2026 and the deadline is 16 Oct 2026 (no extension found). AADE's 15 Sep 2026 update set a 55% minimum KAEK geospatial overlap. The core filing is done on the state tool, which is free, and I found no commercial KYD software. The AADE reminder went to 344,536 producers. The duty is annual, with a short Aug-Oct peak. A parcel-mismatch tracker is a narrow wedge, and the peak ends in a week. Buyers (KYD, agronomists) are few and may not pay. Unverified: private vendors, willingness to pay, and the penalty regime.

Law 4276/2014 art. 2 (as amended by 5121/2024 art. 61) sets up the tourist-business registry (ΜΗ.Τ.Ε.) and the ΕΣΛ/ΒΣΝΠ. Art. 61 only removes the notification-number duty. It sets no renewal, deadline or penalty. The new eΜΗΤΕ/mydigitaltourism platform is a state build funded by the Recovery Fund, so it is out of scope. I found no recurring annual duty or rollout deadline. This was a thin check: 2 searches, 1 fetch, and I did not open the greece20 PDF or mydigitaltourism.gr. It matches the earlier K11 note of no recurring renewal duty, so there is no revive case. The state portal and accountants cover one-off filings. Weak recurring pain, so I keep the score at 3.
